claims.rule: `<cli> help --json` prints one JSON document that names every command.
claims.why: An agent learns the interface from the interface. Help that parses lets it list commands without scraping prose.

evidence.finding: Without help as data an agent, and the X-ray, cannot list the commands or who sees each, so no surface can be checked or trusted; the inventory comparison reads the commands from it.

claims.check: Run `help --json` (then `--help --json`). Pass when stdout is one JSON document with a `commands` array of objects that each have a `name`.
claims.fix: Keep help as data (a COMMANDS table) and print it with `help --json`: { commands: [{ name, effect, summary, usage[] }], exitCodes: [{ code, meaning }] }.

claims.rule: Help says who sees each command: only the person, or other people.
claims.why: The one thing an agent must know before acting is whether other people will see it.

evidence.finding: An agent that cannot tell which commands reach other people can send what it meant to draft.

claims.check: Each command in `help --json` has `effect` of `private` or `others`.
claims.fix: Add `effect: "private" | "others"` to every command in help JSON, from one action catalog, and group the text help under two headings.

claims.rule: Every command the CLI registers is listed once in `help --json` and in the inventory the adopter generates from its command registration, and the X-ray covers exactly that set.
claims.why: A conformance report is only as good as its coverage: a command nobody listed is never checked.

evidence.finding: A command missing from the inventory is never checked, so an untested surface passes as conforming; a duplicate hides which declaration runs.

claims.check: Compare the commands in `help --json` with `--inventory <file>` (`{ "cli": [names] }`). Fail on a name missing from either side or listed twice; skip without an inventory.
claims.fix: Generate the inventory from the CLI's own command registration (its dispatcher's table), never by hand, and declare every registered command.

claims.rule: Every command answers `<command> --help` with exit 0 on stdout, and nothing on stderr.
claims.why: An agent asks the command itself, at the point of use; it should not need a separate document.

evidence.source: docs/decisions/2026-10-30-ouro-ax/evidence/eval-baseline.md
evidence.finding: Every baseline run started with `--help` and most read a command's help before using it (1 to 5 help calls per run); no run failed for want of it.

claims.check: Run `<command> --help` for every listed command.
claims.fix: Route `<command> --help` to the command's own help page before parsing its arguments.

claims.rule: No help line is wider than the width limit (100 columns by default).
claims.why: Long lines wrap unpredictably in terminals and transcripts and cost tokens to re-read.

evidence.source: The first adopter's AX principles; its help's width limit
evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown agents failing without it yet.

claims.check: Measure every line of `--help` and each `<command> --help`.
claims.fix: Wrap help at one width in the help renderer, not by hand.

claims.rule: The overview (`--help`) fits one screen: at most 60 lines.
claims.why: The overview is read on every cold start; details belong on each command's page.

evidence.source: The first adopter's help: its overview's line limit
evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown agents failing without it yet.

claims.check: Count the lines of `--help`.
claims.fix: Keep one line per command in the overview and move details to `<command> --help`.

claims.rule: Exit codes are documented, and every exit code the CLI gives is one of them.
claims.why: Stable, documented exit codes let an agent branch without parsing prose.

evidence.finding: An exit code the help does not document breaks every caller that branches on the code: a script or agent reads an undocumented code as the wrong outcome.

claims.check: Read `exitCodes` from help JSON (or an `Exit codes:` line), then compare every exit code seen during the X-ray.
claims.fix: Keep one exit-code table, print it in help and help JSON, and exit only with codes from it.

claims.rule: Every read takes `--json` and prints exactly one JSON document (a stream prints JSON lines), exits 0 and writes nothing to stderr.
claims.why: One parseable answer per call is the cheapest thing for an agent to consume.

evidence.source: Ouro UI design record of 2026-10-11 (CLI kit); the first adopter's help: --json on every read
evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown agents failing without it yet.

claims.check: Run each read command's argument-free usage (or with one harvested ref) with `--json`.
claims.fix: Give the read a `--json` that prints the same data the text shows, as one document.

claims.rule: Ambiguous verbs (edit, delete, remove) don't act; they answer with the specific commands.
claims.why: `edit` could mean a private draft or a message others already saw; guessing is how agents do the wrong thing.

evidence.finding: An ambiguous verb that acts can pick the effect other people see when the person meant a private one (`edit` a draft or a sent message). Agents in the probes read help first and never tried bare `edit`, so this rests on the hazard.

claims.check: Run `edit`, `delete` and `remove` when they are not listed commands. Pass when each fails and names at least one listed command.
claims.fix: Answer each ambiguous verb with one line naming the private command and the one others see.

claims.rule: Every command other people see refuses to run without `--why`, and says so.
claims.why: What others see is logged with who asked and why.

evidence.finding: An action other people see without a stated reason cannot be attributed to who asked, so the person cannot audit what their agent did in their name.

claims.check: Run each others-see command with a made-up target and no `--why`.
claims.fix: Check `--why` first in every others-see command and refuse with the usage exit code.

claims.rule: A wrong reference fails before anything reaches anyone, and the error says where to get a right one.
claims.why: Checking before acting keeps a stale id from becoming a wrong message.

evidence.finding: A stale or wrong reference that is not refused before acting sends a message to the wrong people.

claims.check: Run each others-see command with `--why` and a target that does not exist.
claims.fix: Resolve the target first; on a miss, name the command that lists valid ones.

claims.rule: Every command other people see has a preview that acts on nothing (`--dry-run`) and names who will see it.
claims.why: An agent, or a checker, can confirm the audience without acting; a wall it is not, because nothing waits on it.

evidence.finding: Without a preview that acts on nothing, the only way to learn who will see an action is to do it. No agent in the probes used --dry-run, so this rests on the hazard, not on a run.

claims.check: When `<command> --help` mentions `--dry-run`, run it on a real target with `--why`. Pass when it exits 0, names who will see it, and nothing changes.
claims.fix: Add `--dry-run`: resolve the target, print the preview line ("Would send to X as the person. Everyone in X will see it."), exit 0, and send nothing.

claims.rule: A command that takes free text accepts it as one argument, not only on stdin, and its help shows that form.
claims.why: An agent allowed to run only this CLI (`shell(<cli>)`) cannot pipe into it: the pipe's first command is not the CLI, so the call is denied.

evidence.finding: On the first adopter's main branch at ffdecc01 text went in only on stdin; the recommended allow-list `shell(app)` denied `printf ... | app ...` and T3 and T4 failed 0 of 2 each. With `--text` and `--file` (6297c319, eval-after-440.md) both went to 2 of 2 with nothing denied.

claims.check: For each usage that reads text from stdin (`-`), look for a usage of the same command with a placeholder in that place. For a command others see that offers --dry-run, the preview probe passes the text as an argument.
claims.fix: Accept the text as an argument and list that usage first; keep `-` for stdin.

claims.rule: A wait command accepts the refs the reads list: `watch <ref>` waits on the conversation a list gave.
claims.why: Waiting through the interface beats polling; when the wait refuses the ref the agent holds, agents fall back to blind streams and pollers.

evidence.source: docs/decisions/2026-10-30-ouro-ax/evidence/eval-baseline.md
evidence.finding: On the first adopter's main branch at ffdecc01 `watch r82dfi` and `watch conversation:r82dfi` exited 2 (watch took only meeting refs) and T5 passed 1 of 2; with a wait on the conversation ref T5 passed 2 of 2 in the X-ray probe (xray-v2-results.md) and the outcomes probe (outcomes-results.md).

claims.check: When the CLI has a `watch` or `wait` command, run it on a harvested conversation ref with a short timeout. Pass on exit 0 or the documented waited-and-nothing-happened code; fail on a usage error.
claims.fix: Let the wait take every ref a read prints, and exit with a documented code when nothing happens in time.

claims.rule: A wait's `--json` answer is a wait (`wait/1`): what happened, or, when nothing did in time, the cursor and the exact command that resumes.
claims.why: A typed wait tells an agent what happened, or exactly how to keep waiting, so it never writes its own polling loop.

evidence.source: docs/decisions/2026-10-30-ouro-ax/evidence/outcomes-results.md
evidence.finding: With a typed wait on the conversation T5 passed 2 of 2 in 4.5 calls and 110k tokens, against 1 of 2 in 8 calls and 254k tokens on main.

claims.fix: Answer waits with `ax-wait` (`waitFor({ ... })`), which gives the cursor and the resume command.

claims.rule: Reads change nothing.
claims.why: An agent must be able to look freely.

evidence.finding: A read that writes changes what other people see (a read receipt, a log row) while the agent only looked, and makes looking unsafe.

claims.check: Snapshot the state commands before and after every read the X-ray makes (including the flag probes); compare.
claims.fix: Keep reads free of writes (no mark-read, no log row, no cache eviction others see).

claims.rule: A refused call changes nothing, except an audit record that says it was refused.
claims.why: An agent that gets the call wrong must be able to try again safely.

evidence.finding: A refusal that leaves a partial write makes a retry unsafe: the corrected call can duplicate what the refused one half did.

claims.check: Snapshot the state commands around each refused probe of what other people see. Pass when nothing changed, or when every added record mentions the refusal and nothing was removed.
claims.fix: Refuse before writing anything; if you log the refusal, say so in the record (`send.refused`).

claims.rule: The interface records an attributed work event (`work-event/1`) for each action, handoff and wait, and an agent can read them through the interface.
claims.why: The person sees what their agents did in their name, and the work can be measured per plan item.

evidence.source: docs/decisions/2026-10-30-ouro-ax/evidence/flow-probe.md
evidence.finding: With a value-stream view over work events, agents named the item that took the most agent time in its lane in 2 of 2 runs (0 of 2 without it); the events did not change success on the five core tasks.

claims.check: With `--events "<args>"`, read the events the CLI lists and validate each against `work-event/1`; skip without it.
claims.fix: Emit `workEventOf(outcome, { ... })` at the shared action dispatcher and list the events with a read command.
